title: Refresh and Close in the same place in every side panel
summary: Folders, Search, To-do, Calendar and Contents each have a Refresh button next to Close, in the same spot.
details: fa-rotate::Refresh reloads that tab’s own data without reloading the page: the folder tree, the current search, your tasks, the calendar, the headings of the page.
The two buttons no longer move when you switch tabs, and the panel keeps the room for its scroll bar.
In Contents, Print and PDF are in the header, and the select bar at the bottom keeps the count, Copy and Clear.
imageAlt: The top of the Contents side panel with the Refresh and Close buttons in the top corner, where every side panel has them

title: Print and PDF match the sheet on screen
summary: A spreadsheet prints and exports as the grid you see. When a table is wider than the page you are asked how to print it: fit to the page, landscape, or split.
details: fa-print::Print and PDF sit in the Contents panel header, also with nothing ticked: they take the whole entry, or only the ticked sections.

fa-table::When the entry has a table wider than the page, Print and PDF first ask Wide tables: Fit to page width (smaller text, the default choice), Landscape page for wide tables, or Actual size, split across pages (the first column, row numbers and header row repeat on every page). Tick Remember my choice to stop being asked; Change wide table setting in the Export menu or the PDF window asks again.
Empty rows and columns at the end of a sheet are not printed, and rows are only as high as their text. Hidden columns and rows, scrollbars and toolbars are left out too.

Ctrl+P cannot ask: it uses your remembered choice, else fit to the page. Firefox cannot switch a single page to landscape when printing: there a wide table is fitted to the portrait width. The PDF file has landscape pages in every browser.
imageAlt: The Contents panel in Select mode; Print and PDF in its header act on the ticked sections

title: A short “What’s new” popup after login
summary: Once after you sign in, a small window lists the features you have not seen yet.
details: fa-star::The popup shows only what is new since you last saw it, the most important features first. Closing it in any way (Got it, the X, Esc or a click outside) counts as seen, on every browser and after the next login.
fa-link::“and N more” opens the full What’s new page.
fa-toggle-off::“Don’t show these popups” turns it off. Settings > Appearance > What’s new has a switch to turn it back on.
imageAlt: The What’s new popup after login: a short list of the newest features with a Got it button

title: Deadline reminders as a small chip
summary: A small clock with a number sits at the top right; click it to see the tasks due soon. It folds away by itself.
details: fa-clock::The reminder no longer covers the page. The chip shows how many tasks are due soon.
Click the chip to open the list. A task from a step links to it. Esc, the title or Collapse fold it again after a few seconds on its own; Dismiss all clears the list.
The chip stays the way you left it for the rest of the session, so it does not open itself on every page.
imageAlt: The small round reminder chip at the top right of the page with the number of deadlines coming up, and the list it opens

title: Print or export only the sections you pick
summary: Tick sections in the Contents panel, then Print or PDF gives just those, with spreadsheets drawn as grids.
details: fa-list-check::In the Contents panel, press Select and tick the sections you want. Print and PDF in the panel header then use only those.
fa-file-pdf::PDF makes a file with only the ticked sections (and the headings above them). The Export as PDF window says when a selection is active. With nothing ticked you get the whole entry.
Spreadsheets print and export like the grid on screen: grid lines, grey row and column labels, fills and bold kept, rows never split over a page, empty filler columns and rows left out.
Plain tables made in the text editor are not spreadsheets and stay ordinary tables.
imageAlt: The Contents panel in Select mode with two headings ticked, Print and PDF in its header

title: Spreadsheets in the text show all of their columns
summary: The frame is as wide as the table, or scrolls to the real last column with a bar you can see.
details: A spreadsheet in an experiment is no longer cut off at the right. If it fits, the frame is exactly its width; if not, a scroll bar under it reaches the last column.
The row of column letters is as high as the other rows, and no empty strip is left above the header or under the last row.
Text in a column that was never sized by hand is fitted to the text and starts at the left.
imageAlt: A spreadsheet in the text of an experiment showing all five of its columns and its rows inside the text frame

title: Browse folders like a file explorer
summary: The Folders panel shows a tree, a list or cards, with a path bar, and you move things by dragging.
details: The buttons at the top of the Folders panel switch between Tree, List and Cards. Your choice is remembered.
List and Cards open one folder at a time. A path bar under the list shows where you are: click any part of it to go back up.
Drag a file or a folder onto a folder to move it. A message with Undo appears. You can only move what you are allowed to edit.
Exp, Res and All choose which entries the panel shows.
The Create window has a Folder choice too, so a new entry can start in a folder.
imageAlt: The Folders panel in list view with the Favourites, Tree, List and Cards view buttons at the top

title: Five ways to see experiments and resources
summary: Choose Cards, Compact rows, Rows with preview, Board by status or Tabular. Your choice is saved with your account.
details: The buttons above the list switch the layout. Cards is the full card for each entry; Compact rows is one line each, grouped by month.
Rows with preview shows the list on the left and the entry you pick on the right. Use the arrow keys to move through the entries.
Board by status puts the entries in columns, one for each status.
Tabular is a table you can sort. Experiments and resources each keep their own choice.
The choice is saved with your account, so it is the same in another browser.
imageAlt: The row of layout buttons above the experiments list, next to the sort buttons, with the list below

title: A clearer dashboard
summary: Four tiles at the top, counts on the category and status chips, and one Create button on each card.
details: The tiles show experiments and resources you changed this week, and your open steps and open tasks. A tile opens exactly what it counts.
The category and status chips under Experiments and Resources show how many entries each one has. A chip with no entries is dimmed.
Experiments, Resources and (for admins) Announcements each have the same Create button at the right of the card title.
The Scheduled bookings card is hidden.
imageAlt: The dashboard: tiles with the number of experiments and resources modified this week, open steps and open tasks, above the experiment, resource and announcement cards

title: Choose a folder when you create
summary: The Create window has a Folder choice on every page, and the command palette opens the same window.
details: Press Create on the dashboard or in a list, use the plus in the top bar, or choose New experiment or New resource in the command palette (Ctrl+K). The same window opens.
Folder lists Unfiled first, then your folders. Use the tabs to show My folders, Bookmarked or All folders, and New folder to make one on the spot.
The window starts on the folder you have open, or on the folder of the entry you created last. Starting from a template, the folder you choose wins.
A new entry opens in edit mode, as before.
imageAlt: The Create dialog with the Experiment, Resource and template tabs, the title field and the Folder chooser

title: Calmer entry pages
summary: Goals, Conclusion and Notes are tiles under the title, and Save and go back always returns to the view page.
details: The Goals, Conclusion and Notes of an experiment show as three tiles under its title. In edit mode you type in them directly.
The buttons under the tiles are flat and quiet. The less common actions are under the three dots.
On the edit page, Save keeps your changes and Save and go back saves and opens the view page of the entry.
The editor toolbar is one row. The three dots at its end open the rest of the buttons.
imageAlt: An experiment page: title with category and status, the toolbar, the details block and the main text with its headings

title: Print a label
summary: Print a label from the plus menu: your own text, one label per row of a pasted table, on the label sizes your admins set up.
details: Open the plus in the top bar and choose Print a label. Pick a format, type up to eight lines of text and press Print. A preview shows the label with dashed lines for the margins.
Write a name in curly brackets, for example {sample}, where a value changes: it becomes a box you fill in.
Format each line: size, bold, italic and left, centre or right.
To print many labels, paste cells from a spreadsheet and click the columns you want. Each row is one label.

Fisher (37 x 15 mm) is the first format by default. An admin adds or changes formats and sets the printer in Admin panel, Labels: the address and port of the printer, its resolution and the web address for the QR code.
Printing goes to the label printer of the lab over the network. It needs the printer address, which only an admin can set.
imageAlt: The Print a label window with the label format, copies, the preview with dashed margins and the lines of text

title: Google Calendar and Google Tasks
summary: Link a project to a Google calendar, choose the calendar of each task, and keep your choices in every browser.
details: The gear in the To-do panel (and the Settings button of the calendar page) opens Calendar settings: working hours and weekend days, the Google settings, calendars from a web address, and a private link for other calendar apps.
Link a project to a Google calendar in the Calendars menu of the calendar page. The tasks of the project go to that calendar. A calendar you choose for one task wins over the project's.
Choose which calendars are shown in the Calendars menu. Google calendars show next to your projects.
Your calendar view, hidden projects and Google choices are saved with your account and follow you to another browser. The Google sign-in itself stays in the browser.

Google Tasks sync of the to-do list is optional and off by default. It runs in your browser and needs an admin to switch it on: set GOOGLE_SYNC_CSP=true in the server settings and restart, which lets the page use Google sign-in. This was only tested with a stand-in for Google, not a real account.
imageAlt: The Calendar settings window opened from the gear in the To-do panel, with working hours, the Google section with Connect Google, calendars from a web address and the private link

title: Mind map of a project
summary: The brain button in Boards turns a project into a mind map of cards and arrows.
details: Press the brain button in the Boards toolbar (Open the mind map) to switch between the columns and the mind map. Your choice is saved with your account.
A card is a question, a task or an experiment. Subprojects are nested inside their project. Arrows connect cards, and a card stays where you drag it.
An experiment card shows its goals, conclusions and notes, read from the experiment's own fields.

A task card follows its task: move the task to another project and the card goes with it. The map refreshes by itself, and the Refresh button reloads it. A card has a button to remove it from the map.
A card's popup is only as tall as its content.
imageAlt: The Boards page as a mind map: question, experiment and task cards joined by arrows inside the project frame

title: Give a step to a colleague
summary: Type @ in a step to assign it. Whoever ticks it, it is done for everybody.
details: Type @ in a step and pick a name. You become the assigner and each person you mention gets a to-do of their own, linked to the entry, with the step's deadline.
When any one of them ticks their to-do, or anyone with edit rights ticks the step, the step is completed for everybody.
You and the other people the step was given to are told when it is completed. Nobody else on the experiment is.
The same @ list works in comments: the person you mention is told if they can read the entry.
A step with a deadline shows in the To-do panel and on that day in the Activity calendar.
imageAlt: The Steps and tasks section of an experiment: two steps with tick boxes and deadlines, then the Data, Links and Local files sections

title: Back to the folder, and a folder path with subfolders
summary: Back and Save and go back return to the folder an entry is in, and a path bar at the bottom lets you move up or down the folders.
details: In a folder's list, and under an experiment or resource that is in a folder, a bar shows the path, for example Cloning > Plasmids. Click any part to open that folder.
When the folder has subfolders, the last button opens a menu of them to go one level down. The bar stays at the bottom of the window as you scroll.
The back arrow (also on the edit page) and Save and go back now return to that folder.
imageAlt: The folder path bar at the bottom of an experiment, Cloning then Plasmids, with the experiment text above it

title: Well plates: switch views, copy, and Excel-style formulas
summary: Switch a plate between plate and spreadsheet, recolour it by any column, copy it as a new plate, and paste formulas with moving references.
details: On a page you are reading, a well plate has Plate and Spreadsheet buttons and Colour by and Label by lists. They only change what you see; nothing is saved.
The copy button in a plate's header copies the whole plate; paste it into the text to get a new plate.
Pasting a copied formula in a spreadsheet moves its references like Excel, and pasting and resizing rows or columns are part of Undo.
Printing from the edit page no longer puts plates and tables on top of each other.
imageAlt: A well plate in an experiment: the Plate and Spreadsheet switch and the copy button above the wells

title: Link an experiment to its data folder
summary: Attach the network folder where an experiment's raw data lives, and open it from the entry in one click.
details: In the Data section of an experiment, paste a network share path (smb://server/share/folder or \\server\share\folder), add an optional label such as "Raw data folder", and press Add.
Each link has buttons to open it on a Mac, to copy the Windows path to paste into Explorer, and to insert a reference to it in the main text.
The label keeps a long path readable. Remove a link with the trash icon while editing.
imageAlt: The Data section of an experiment with a network folder link labelled Raw data folder and the path and label fields to add another

title: Quick links to LabCollector and your lab's tools
summary: The Links menu in the top bar opens LabCollector and your lab's own pages in one click.
details: Open Links in the top bar to reach LabCollector, OpenIRIS, MoorLab Wiki, ETHIS and MoorLab Zoom. They open in a new tab.
A team admin can change any of these addresses with the pencil icon next to it, so the link always points to the right place.
imageAlt: The More menu in the top bar with Orders and other links

title: Link templates and see which version you used
summary: Record the template an experiment follows, with or without inserting its content, and keep track of its versions.
details: In an experiment, open Search in the left sidebar and set Type to Experiment templates.
Press Link to associate the template with the experiment without inserting anything, or Add to text to insert its content at the cursor.
Associated templates are listed under Links, each with its version number and how many times it was inserted. Click one to open the template.
Open a template to see its version history and restore an older version; the other versions are kept.
imageAlt: The Search panel with Experiment templates selected: each template has a button to link it to the experiment and a button to add its text

title: Faster scrolling with several spreadsheets
summary: Spreadsheets near the screen now appear as a light preview and become fully editable the moment you click them.
details: Only the table you click gets the full editor, so scrolling past many tables stays smooth.
The preview matches the editor's look, column widths and row heights, so nothing jumps when you click.
The cell you clicked is selected straight away, and the table you are editing stays live while you scroll.
imageAlt: A spreadsheet in the text of an experiment with the small bar above it for collapsing, fitting and copying

title: Tab and Shift+Tab indent several list lines at once
summary: Select multiple bullet or numbered lines and press Tab to indent them all, or Shift+Tab to outdent them.
details: Works for bullet lists, numbered lists and several selected paragraphs.
Nested lists move one level per press.
imageAlt: Three numbered lines selected in the editor; pressing Tab indents all of them together

title: Version history for templates
summary: See every saved version of a template, compare revisions, and restore an older one without losing the current one.
details: The history opens in a popup on the edit page.
Restoring a version makes it current and keeps the other versions.
Each version has its own edit history that you can restore individually.
imageAlt: The Version history window of a template listing its saved versions with who and when, and buttons to restore one

title: Insert a spreadsheet of any size, and handier tools in view mode
summary: Drag across a grid to choose the size, like Insert table. View mode now has copy-table and auto-fit buttons.
details: Spreadsheet is also in the classic Insert menu.
Copy the whole table in one click, and auto-fit rows or columns to their content.
Row heights now grow when a narrower column needs more wrapped lines.
imageAlt: The Insert menu of the editor with Spreadsheet open: a grid where you point at the number of columns and rows

title: Project management is now Boards, with richer cards
summary: Tasks are now cards, with status badges, deadlines, linked experiments and resources, and bulk actions.
details: Cards show each linked experiment or resource with its status colour.
Select several cards to archive or delete them together.
Steps and comments can be collapsed, and deadlines show how urgent they are.
Duplicate a card into another project, and open a card straight into edit mode.
imageAlt: The Boards page with the Plasmid project tab, the card filters and the To do column with demo cards and deadlines

title: Smoother ordering
summary: Attachments can be reused, orders can advance and archive themselves, and notes support lists.
details: Reuse an attachment across orders, and download it with its own button.
Orders can move from requested to ordered when a procurement ID appears, and archive after a set time.
Notes support bulleted and numbered lists, and long titles and file names wrap properly.
imageAlt: The Orders page with the request form on the left and the list of orders with their status on the right

title: More reliable spreadsheet editing
summary: Formulas, fill-drag, undo and cell formatting behave more predictably, in both the inline editor and the popup.
details: Fill-drag keeps absolute references (the ones written with a dollar sign) fixed, so a formula copied down still points at the same cell.
Undo in a spreadsheet only undoes spreadsheet edits, and undo in the text leaves tables alone.
Tab and Enter move between cells, and selected cells and fill-drag are clearly highlighted.
Fixed cell formatting in the popup and a case where saving could blank cells.

Add rows: under a spreadsheet, type how many rows you want and press Add rows to add them at the bottom, up to 400 rows in all. The popup has the same box next to its buttons. Enter never adds a row: in the last row it stays in the cell.
Vertical alignment: select cells and press the top, middle or bottom button next to the left, center, right and justify buttons, in the page and in the popup.
Typing and then adding or deleting a row or column straight away no longer loses what you typed.

Well plates keep their size: rows and columns cannot be added or deleted with Enter, the right-click menu, Add rows or the size boxes, in the page or in the popup. To change the size, pick another plate size in the popup, or choose Custom in its size list to turn the plate into an ordinary spreadsheet.
The cells you select stay selected when you scroll the page.

A plate or spreadsheet shows its row and column labels (1, 2, 3 and A, B, C) before you click it, also for older ones that were saved without them, and rows keep their height when the preview becomes the grid.
A table below the one you add rows to no longer jumps for a moment, and the editor no longer slides a wide plate out of view sideways.
imageAlt: A spreadsheet in edit mode with its tool bar above the grid: undo, redo, add rows and columns, copy and delete

screenshots.caption: A normal spreadsheet has the Add rows bar under it. A well plate keeps its size, so it has none, and both show their row and column labels

title: A tidier top bar
summary: The navigation bar keeps the key icons visible and folds the rest into a More menu.
details: A Links dropdown groups shortcuts.
The LabCollector link keeps its URL editable from the Tools menu.
imageAlt: The More menu in the top bar with Orders and other links

title: Link experiments and resources to your cards
summary: Connect a card to the experiments and resources it is about, and jump between them in one click.
details: Link items while you create a card, or later from the card's detail view.
Use the search panel next to the card to find an experiment or resource, link it, or add it as a step in one move.
Each linked item shows its status colour and type, so you can see at a glance how the work is going.
A project's Linked items section and an All links summary list everything connected to that project, including subprojects.
Click a linked item to open the experiment or resource itself.
imageAlt: The Boards page with the Plasmid project tab, the card filters and the To do column with demo cards and deadlines

title: Better notifications and feedback
summary: You are told when someone gives you access, and the Feedback board can sort by votes or date.
details: Notifications arrive when you gain read access to an experiment or resource, even if you had access before.
The dashboard announcement feed is easier to read.
imageAlt: The notification bell menu listing a step deadline and two to-do deadlines, with Clear all, Notification history and Notification settings below

title: An activity calendar for deadlines and tasks
summary: See every deadline in one calendar: your scheduled tasks together with the unfinished steps of your experiments and resources.
details: Open it from the calendar icon in the left sidebar. A badge counts what is overdue or due within the next hour.
A month grid shows each day's items as small count pills, with clear states for Today, the day you selected, and overdue days. Collapse the grid when you only want the list.
Switch between Day, Week and Month views, and hide weekends if you don't need them. The Today button and 'All visible dates' jump you back or show everything in range.
Below the grid, an agenda lists the items for what you selected, ordered by exact time. Each card says where it came from: a personal task, or a step of an experiment or resource.
Click a step to open its experiment or resource, and mark steps and tasks done right from the agenda, the same way as on the experiment page.
The User and Team switch decides whose experiment and resource steps you see.
Give a task a title, notes, an exact date and time, and a reminder: at the deadline, 15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week before, or a custom number of minutes.
Reminders appear as one grouped, collapsible banner that stays as you move between pages, and they also arrive as notifications and email, following your existing step-deadline preference.
Subscribe to your deadlines from Google Calendar or Apple Calendar with a private link from the Calendar tab. The link is read-only, and you can regenerate or revoke it at any time.
imageAlt: The Activity calendar panel with Day, Week and Month buttons, the November month grid with coloured dots for tasks and experiments, and a list of the dates

title: A left sidebar with your tools one click away
summary: A slim rail on the left keeps folders, search, to-dos and the calendar open next to your work, on every page.
details: Folders: browse and manage your experiment folders, pin a favorite, and collapse branches you don't need.
Search: your saved filters and results, combined in one place.
Quick search and commands: press Ctrl/Cmd + K from anywhere.
To-do list: tasks and step deadlines sorted by due date, with a count of what is due.
Activity calendar: a Day, Week or Month view of deadlines, with your external calendar.
On experiment pages a table of contents tab lists the headings so you can jump around, and filter sections to print or copy.
The rail stays put while you scroll, and the last panel you opened is remembered.
imageAlt: The left sidebar: a column of small buttons for Folders, Search, Quick search, To-do, Calendar and Contents, with the guide button at the bottom

title: Folders and READMEs
summary: A shared tree of folders for experiments and resources, each with a README and its own permissions.
details: fa-folder-tree::Open the Folders button in the left sidebar. Click a folder to list only what is inside it; the number beside it counts its items.
fa-folder-plus::Press New folder, give it a name and pick a parent folder to nest it. Choose the folder when you create an entry or on its edit page.
fa-file-lines::Press the page icon on a folder to open its README. The owner and admins edit it; everyone who can see the folder reads it.
fa-ellipsis-vertical::The three dots on a folder give Export, Edit (rename, move, description), Permissions and Delete. Deleting moves its items to Unfiled.
fa-user-shield::Permissions (owner and admins): set Can see and Can edit as on an entry, tick Include subfolders, press Apply and confirm.
fa-star::Star a folder to bookmark it. The Refresh button at the top of the panel loads the tree again.
imageAlt: The Folders panel with the folder tree of the team: Cell culture, Cloning with Plasmids and Screening, Protein work
purpose: Keep the lab organised in folders the whole team sees, and decide once who can see and edit what is in a folder.
uses: One folder per project, with a README that lists the protocols and naming rules.
A subfolder for each idea you want to test, so the approaches sit side by side.
news: Folders now hold resources as well as experiments, can be bookmarked, have READMEs, can be exported, and can remember permissions that apply to everything inside.
shot: The Folders tab with a project folder open and its README beside it, and the Folder permissions dialog with the Can see tab open

screenshots.caption: The folder README: the owner and admins edit it, and everyone who can see the folder can read it
Folder permissions: the Can see and Can edit tabs, each with a base level and Teams, User Groups and Users to add. Apply asks you to confirm

title: Folder views: tree, list and cards
summary: Browse folders like a file explorer: as a tree, a list with preview, or cards. Drag a file or folder onto a folder to move it.
details: fa-table-list::The buttons at the top of the Folders panel switch between Tree, List and Cards. Your choice is remembered.
fa-layer-group::List and Cards open one folder at a time: click a folder to go in, use the “..” row or the path bar to go back up.
fa-flask::Exp, Res and All choose which entries the panel shows; Unfiled lists entries that are in no folder.
fa-up-down-left-right::Drag a file or folder onto a folder, the “..” row, All (folders only) or Unfiled (files only). A message with Undo appears.
fa-ellipsis::The three dots at the top switch Favourites, Files and Counts on or off. Drag the panel’s right edge to make it narrower.
imageAlt: The Folders panel in list view with the Favourites, Tree, List and Cards view buttons at the top
purpose: Find a folder quickly in a big lab, see what is in it and file work by dragging, without leaving the page.
uses: Switch to Cards to see what each folder holds.
Drag an experiment from Unfiled into its project folder.
news: New: List with a file preview and Cards views, an Exp / Res / All switch, a favourites list, drag to move with Undo, and a panel that can be slim.
shot: The Folders panel in the List view inside a folder, with a file picked and its details below

title: The left sidebar
summary: The slim row of buttons on the left edge: folders, search, quick search, to-do, calendar and contents, one click away.
details: fa-bars::Click a button to open its panel next to your page and click it again to close. The last panel you opened is remembered.
fa-left-right::Drag the right edge of a panel to resize it, or click the edge and press the Left and Right arrow keys.
fa-bolt::Quick search and commands: Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac) on any page. Type to find commands, folders and entries; Enter opens one.
fa-list-check::To-do and Activity calendar show a red number for what is overdue or due soon. Contents appears on entry pages only.
fa-rotate::Every panel has Close and Refresh in the top corner, in the same place. Refresh reloads that panel without leaving the page.
fa-bars::On a narrow window the row folds into one button left of the logo.
imageAlt: The left sidebar: a column of small buttons for Folders, Search, Quick search, To-do, Calendar and Contents, with the guide button at the bottom
purpose: Keep the tools you use all day next to your work and reach anything without hunting through menus.
uses: Keep the To-do panel open and tick off steps as you finish them.
Press Ctrl+K and type a few letters to jump to an entry.
news: One row of buttons with all of these tools on every page, and a keyboard-first quick search and command window.
shot: The left sidebar with the Folders panel open and the row of buttons outlined, and the quick search window open over a page

title: Activity calendar
summary: One calendar for what is coming and what you finished: your tasks, the steps of your experiments and the days you worked.
details: fa-calendar-days::Open the calendar button in the left sidebar. A red number counts what is overdue or due within the hour.
Choose Day, Week or Month. The agenda below the grid lists what you selected in time order and says if an item is a task or a step.
Tasks and steps with a deadline show on their day; finished ones stay on the day you finished them. Click a step to open its experiment.
fa-calendar-day::The Day button in the editor toolbar lists the headings you write after a date on that date.
The User and Team buttons switch between your items and the team’s. Add a task with a date, time and reminder from the panel.
fa-link::Subscribe from Google or Apple Calendar with the private, read-only link on the Calendar tab; you can regenerate or revoke it.
imageAlt: The Activity calendar panel with Day, Week and Month buttons, the November month grid with coloured dots for tasks and experiments, and a list of the dates
purpose: See what is due this week, never miss a step deadline hidden inside an experiment, and look back at earlier days.
uses: Switch to Week view on Monday to see every deadline.
Look back at what you did on a given day.
news: New: an activity calendar that combines tasks and experiment steps, with reminders and calendar subscriptions.
shot: The Activity calendar panel with the month grid, the Day/Week/Month buttons and the agenda below

title: Project Boards
summary: Plan lab work as projects of cards with deadlines and steps, and link each card to its experiments and resources.
details: fa-list-check::Open Boards from the top bar (under More). Create a project, then add cards. A card has notes, a deadline, steps, comments and people.
fa-link::Link experiments and resources from the search panel beside a card; each shows a status dot. All links lists every link of the project.
fa-brain::The brain button switches between columns and a Mind map of cards and arrows. Each project keeps its own map.
Tick several cards to archive or delete them together. Pin to top in a card’s ⋮ menu keeps it at the top of its column.
Drag a project tab to reorder it. A project can hold subprojects. Archive a finished project from its edit dialog.
fa-floppy-disk::Columns or mind map, card size (compact or expanded) of each project and the last project tab are saved with your account.
imageAlt: The Boards page with the Plasmid project tab, the card filters and the To do column with demo cards and deadlines
purpose: Keep track of who does what and by when, with the plan and the experiments pointing at each other.
uses: One board per paper or grant, a card for each series of experiments.
Link a card to the experiments that belong to it.
news: New: the mind map, and your Boards view is remembered.
shot: The Boards page with a project open and one card showing its steps and linked experiments, and the search panel used to link them

title: Orders
summary: Request what the lab needs and follow each order from request to delivery.
details: fa-cart-shopping::Open Orders from the top bar (under More) and press New order. Add supplier, link or catalogue number, notes and attachments.
fa-clone::Copy an order to fill the request form again; use the arrow beside a file (Add to new order) to reuse an attachment.
Status: Requested, Ordered, Collected, In storage, Backlogged or Cancelled. Use the coloured dropdown, or tick several and Move to status.
fa-file-pdf::Drop the signed shop sheet (PDF) on the dashed area at the top: it is attached to the matching orders, and an Ordered one becomes Collected.
fa-clipboard-check::Order Status lists each procurement with its orders and how many items were collected. Templates keep texts such as supplier emails.
fa-thumbtack::Pin an order to keep it at the top. Pinned for all is shared with the team; Reference is only yours. Admins can turn auto-collect off.
imageAlt: The Orders page with the request form on the left and the list of orders with their status on the right
purpose: One place to request what the lab needs and to see where each order is, instead of emails and sticky notes.
uses: Request a reagent with the supplier quote attached.
Drop the signed shop sheet and see the order become Collected.
news: New: drop the signed collection sheets to mark orders Collected and notify the requesters, the Order Status tab with items collected per procurement, and a setting for the collected notification. Received is now called In storage.
shot: The Orders page with a few orders at different stages and one order open

title: Link items to experiments
summary: Connect an experiment to the data folders, resources, orders and templates it relates to.
details: Scroll below the main text. Each section opens and closes on its own.
fa-list-check::Steps and tasks: a checklist with deadlines. Type @ in a step to give it to a colleague (see Steps and tasks).
Data: paste a network path (smb://server/share/folder), add a label and press Add. Buttons open it on a Mac or copy the Windows path.
fa-link::Links: other experiments, resources, orders, templates, web addresses and LabCollector entries.
fa-paperclip::Files / folders and Local files: attach files or refer to files kept elsewhere.
Compounds and Custom fields: record chemicals from the compound database and the extra fields your team defined.
imageAlt: The Links section of an experiment with experiment links, associated experimental templates with their version, and resource links
purpose: Record not only what you did but also what you used, where the data lives and what it relates to.
uses: Link the resource of the meeting where the experiment was planned.
Add the network folder with the raw data.
news: New: the Data section for network folders, and order, template and LabCollector links in these sections.
shot: An experiment page scrolled to the sections under the main text with the Data section open

title: Steps and tasks
summary: Break an experiment into steps, give a step to colleagues with @ and see when it is done.
details: fa-list-check::Steps and tasks sit under the main text. Type a step in the box and press Enter. Tick it when done; drag its handle to reorder.
fa-clock::Open the arrow on a step to set a deadline and a reminder. It then shows in the To-do panel and the Activity calendar.
fa-at::Type @ in a step and pick a name. Each person gets a to-do of their own, linked to the entry, and a notification. You are the assigner.
fa-circle-check::When anyone you gave it to ticks their to-do, or anyone with edit rights ticks the step, it is done for everybody. Unticking reopens it.
fa-bell::You and the other assignees are told when the step is completed, not the person who did it. Choose web or email in Settings > Notifications.
The same @ list works in comments. The Open steps tile on the dashboard counts what you still have to do.
imageAlt: The Steps and tasks section of an experiment: two steps with tick boxes and deadlines, then the Data, Links and Local files sections
purpose: Hand a part of an experiment to a colleague and see when it is done, without chasing them.
uses: Ask a colleague to prepare the buffers and be told when they are ready.
Give a step to two people; it closes for both.
news: New: assign a step with @, the person gets it as a to-do, and finishing it tells you.
shot: An experiment's Steps and tasks section with a step that mentions two people, next to one of their to-do lists showing it

title: Templates and their versions
summary: Link a template to an experiment, see which version you used and restore older versions.
details: In Search (left sidebar) set Type to Experiment templates. Link records the template; Add to text inserts its content.
Associated templates are listed under Links with their version and how often they were inserted.
fa-code-branch::Press Publish new version in a template’s toolbar. Versions are numbered and never overwritten.
fa-clock-rotate-left::Version history lists each version with who and when. Edit a version’s name and notes; Restore makes the template look like it did then.
fa-code-compare::Tick two entries and press Compare revisions. Each version also has an Edit history you can restore from.
fa-star::Star the templates you use most to find them quickly.
imageAlt: The Experiment templates page listing two templates, PCR reaction setup and Western blot
purpose: Start from the lab’s standard protocol and know exactly which version of it an experiment followed.
uses: Publish a new version when the standard protocol changes.
See which experiments used version 2.
news: New: template versions with names and notes, version history, restoring a version or a single edit, and template links on experiments.
shot: The template version history with the list of versions and the Restore buttons

title: Feedback board
summary: Post ideas and bugs, upvote what matters and discuss it with your team.
details: fa-lightbulb::Open Feedback from the top bar and post an idea or a problem with a title and a description.
fa-star::Choose Feature or Bug. The two buttons above the list also filter it.
fa-caret-up::Upvote the items that matter to you; you upvote your own post automatically. Sort by Most votes or by date.
fa-comment::Open an item to comment; type @ and a name to mention a colleague.
fa-pen::The author or a team admin can edit an item, change its type and status (open, planned, done or declined) and delete it.
imageAlt: The Feedback board with the form to post a feature idea or a bug and the filter buttons
purpose: Tell the people who run the system what would help, and see what the team cares about most.
uses: Ask for a new field and see how many colleagues want it too.
Report something that does not work and follow it.
news: New: a feedback board with votes, statuses and comments.
shot: The Feedback board sorted by votes, with one item open and its comments

title: Search, favourite filters and linking
summary: Search with your favourite filters, then attach what you find to an experiment or paste a link, without leaving the page.
details: fa-magnifying-glass::Open Search in the left sidebar, pick a Type (All, Experiments, Resources, Experiment templates, Resource templates) and type.
Tick filters (categories, tags, statuses, owners) and press Apply filters. Manage chooses your favourites, saved with your account.
fa-link::While editing, press the link button on a result to attach it under Links, or the second button to paste a link into the text.
For templates, the link button records the template and the second button inserts its content.
With a board card open, results also have buttons to link them to the card or add them as a step.
imageAlt: The Search panel in the left sidebar with its search box, the Exp, Res and All buttons and the results grouped by experiments and resources
purpose: Stop re-entering the same filters, and link what you find into your work in one click.
uses: Favourite your tags and statuses, then filter “my running experiments” in two clicks.
Attach a resource while you edit.
news: New: filters you can favourite, shared by search across experiments, resources and templates, plus attach and paste-a-link buttons on every result.
shot: The Search panel next to an experiment being edited, with the attach and paste-a-link buttons on a result outlined

title: Table of contents in experiments
summary: A list of the headings of an entry to jump around, show only the sections you pick and print or export just those.
details: fa-bars-staggered::On an entry open Contents in the left sidebar. Click a heading to jump to it; levels show by indent and weight.
Type in Filter headings and press Enter to add a filter; with several, choose All or Any. Tables and pictures can be hidden.
fa-square-check::Select turns the rows into tick boxes: click to tick, Shift-click for a range, Select all or None. The entry then shows only those sections.
fa-print::Print and PDF in the panel header act on the ticked sections, or on the whole entry when nothing is ticked. The PDF window says so.
fa-copy::Copy, in the bar at the bottom, copies the ticked sections. Clear drops the selection.
fa-rotate::Refresh and Close sit in the top corner of the panel, as on every side panel.
imageAlt: The Contents panel with the headings of the experiment, ticks for each section, and Print and PDF buttons in its header
purpose: Long experiments become easy to move through, and you can share just the part someone needs.
uses: Print only the Results of a long experiment for a meeting.
Copy the Methods into an email.
news: New: Print, PDF and Copy for the sections you tick.
shot: An experiment with the Table of Contents panel open, three headings ticked in the list and only those sections shown

title: Notifications
summary: The bell tells you what needs you, so you do not have to check every page.
details: fa-bell::The bell in the top bar collects your notifications and shows how many are new.
fa-user-check::You are told when you get access to an entry, are mentioned, are assigned a task, card or step, or an order changes.
fa-gear::Settings > Notifications: every kind has a Web switch (the bell) and an Email switch. The top row switches all kinds at once.
fa-envelope::Turn Email off to get a kind only in the app, or Web off to get it only by email.
imageAlt: The notification bell menu listing a step deadline and two to-do deadlines, with Clear all, Notification history and Notification settings below
purpose: Be told when something changes for you, without checking every page.
uses: Be told right away when someone shares an experiment with you.
Get an email for a step someone gave you.
news: New: notifications for assignments, mentions and access.
shot: The notifications dropdown open from the bell in the top bar

title: The editor toolbar
summary: The buttons above the text of an entry: save, one Insert menu, dates, titles, notes, checklists and spreadsheets.
details: fa-floppy-disk::Save keeps your changes and shows when they were saved; Save and go back opens the view page. File has the Print entries.
fa-plus::Insert is one menu: note, divider, tables, spreadsheet, well plate, image, links and template. Title and Day have their own buttons.
fa-calendar-day::Day inserts today’s date and links your notes to the Activity calendar. The arrow gives Custom date and Log entry (date and time).
fa-heading::Insert title sets text, style and how it shows in Contents; Ctrl+Alt+T opens it. Save style keeps a style for later.
fa-list-check::Checklist: type [ ] and a space for tick boxes. Format painter and Clear formatting sit by the colour buttons.
fa-keyboard::Ctrl+Shift+D date and time, Ctrl+Alt+T title, Ctrl+Alt+N note, Ctrl+Shift+H line. The three dots at the end hold buttons that do not fit.
imageAlt: The editor of an experiment with its menu bar and the toolbar: Save, Insert, formatting, colours, lists and indent buttons
purpose: Find every editing tool in one place and write and structure an experiment faster.
uses: Use Log entry in the Day arrow each time you return, so your notes read as a diary.
Save a title style and apply it to other headings.
news: New: one Insert menu (note, divider, tables, spreadsheets, well plates, links and templates), a Note options button that appears while a note is selected, Spreadsheet tools that appear while a spreadsheet is selected, checklists, and a format painter next to the colours.
shot: The editor toolbar with the Insert menu open

screenshots.caption: Note options appears on the toolbar while your cursor is inside a note
Note options: change the note's title, whether it is in the Table of Contents, and the heading level
Spreadsheet tools appears while a spreadsheet is selected: edit and format it from here. A well plate below has its size fixed, so it has no Add rows bar

title: Spreadsheets and well plates
summary: Put a spreadsheet or well plate in the text, fill it like a normal sheet and keep a plate layout fixed.
details: fa-plus::Insert > Spreadsheet: drag over the squares for a size, or Custom. Well plate gives a 6 to 384-well plate. Click a table to work in it.
fa-keyboard::Tab moves to the next cell, Enter down, Shift+Enter opens the Spreadsheet Editor. Add rows under the table; right-click a header for more.
fa-calculator::Start a cell with = for a formula, such as =A1+B1. Drag the fill handle to copy it; a $ keeps a reference fixed.
fa-circle-dot::A well plate keeps its size and shows round wells. Plate and Spreadsheet switch views; Colour by recolours; the copy button duplicates it.
fa-print::Print and PDF show the sheet like the grid you see. Choose how wide sheets print in the PDF window (see Print and PDF).
fa-rotate-left::Ctrl+Z in a spreadsheet undoes spreadsheet edits only. A sheet wider than the page has a scroll bar under it.
imageAlt: A spreadsheet in edit mode with its tool bar above the grid: undo, redo, add rows and columns, copy and delete
purpose: Record plate layouts, measurements and calculations next to your notes, in a table that behaves like a spreadsheet.
uses: Insert a 96-well plate and type sample names into the wells.
Add a formula to calculate each concentration of a dilution series.
news: New: pick a colour and it applies as you choose it, the formula and formatting bars stay as you left them, and Undo and Redo cover typing, formatting, added rows and columns, and sizes.
shot: The Insert menu with the squares for picking a spreadsheet size

screenshots.caption: Spreadsheet tools appears while a spreadsheet is selected. The well plate below has no Add rows bar, because its size is fixed
A normal spreadsheet has the Add rows bar under it. A well plate keeps its size, so it has none. Both show their row and column labels
The table’s toolbar, the formatting bar (fill and text colours, font, alignment) and the formula bar, open above a spreadsheet

title: Working together: members, assignments and comments
summary: Add colleagues to a project, assign cards to people and talk about the work in comments with @mentions.
details: fa-user-group::Open a project’s edit dialog and use Team members on this project. Remove someone with the × on their name.
A subproject starts with the members of its parent.
fa-user::Open a card and choose people under Assigned to. Each gets a notification; Assigned to me above the board shows only your cards.
fa-comment::Every card has Comments. Type @ and a name to mention someone; they are notified. Cards show a comment count.
The same comments work on tasks in the To-do list and on posts in Feedback. You can edit or delete your own.
imageAlt: The Boards page with the Plasmid project tab, the card filters and the To do column with demo cards and deadlines
purpose: See who is working on a project and who looks after each card, with the conversation next to the work.
uses: Add the project team once, then assign each card.
Mention a colleague in a card comment.
news: New: project members, several people per card, comments with @mentions, and notifications when you are assigned or mentioned.
shot: A card open with the Assigned to field and the Comments section showing an @mention

title: To-do list
summary: Your tasks and the deadlines of your experiment steps in one list: add, remind, repeat, tick off and look back.
details: fa-list-check::Open the checklist button in the left sidebar. Tasks and steps with a deadline are grouped Overdue, Today, Tomorrow, later days.
fa-plus::Type a task in the top box and press Enter. The arrow beside it adds notes, a board project, date, time and reminder.
Reminders: at the deadline, 15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week before, or a time you choose. They need a date and time.
fa-repeat::Repeat: Daily, Weekly, Every weekday, Monthly, Yearly or Custom. Completing a repeating task creates the next one.
Click a title for notes, linked items, steps and comments. Archive, Duplicate and Delete are at the bottom of the details.
fa-calendar::The Calendar tab shows a month and has Create private link for Google or Apple Calendar. Calendar settings are under the gear.
imageAlt: The To-do panel with the tabs Tasks and steps, the add-task field and overdue tasks and steps listed by date
purpose: Know what is due today and never lose a step deadline inside an experiment.
uses: Add a task with a reminder the moment you think of it.
Set a weekly task to repeat on Monday.
news: New: one list for tasks and step deadlines with reminders, steps and comments on tasks, linked items, a completed and archived history, a calendar view, and a calendar subscription.
shot: The To-do panel open next to a page, with the add-task box and the groups Overdue, Today and Tomorrow

screenshots.caption: Adding a task that repeats every week on Monday and Thursday: Repeat, with a Today button next to the date

title: Announcements
summary: Lab news on your dashboard: read it, react to it and look back at earlier announcements.
details: fa-bullhorn::The Announcements card is on the dashboard. A New badge shows until you have seen one, and a notification tells you when one is posted.
A blue circle marks information, a warning triangle something that needs attention, a pin an announcement kept at the top.
Click the title to open it on its own page; Show more reads a long text.
fa-face-smile::React with the face button under an announcement; you can pick several.
See previous announcements lists older ones. Team admins add announcements with the plus button, and can edit and pin them.
imageAlt: The Announcements card of the dashboard with a pinned freezer maintenance notice and a lab meeting notice
purpose: Make sure everyone hears about lab news and changes, without emails getting lost.
uses: Read the latest lab news when you open the dashboard.
Pin the lab meeting schedule so it stays on top.
news: New: an announcement feed on the dashboard with reactions, pinning, pictures and files.
shot: The dashboard with the Announcements feed on the right, showing a pinned announcement and its reactions

title: Experiments
summary: Where your experiments live: create them, find them and act on them.
details: fa-flask::Open Experiments from the top bar or the dashboard. Create opens the Create window: type, title and folder.
fa-magnifying-glass::Search above the list or in the left sidebar. Filter by category, status, owner, date, tags and custom fields, and sort.
fa-table-cells-large::The layout buttons above the list switch Cards, Compact rows, Rows with preview, Board by status and Tabular (see Layouts of the lists).
fa-square-check::Tick several to archive, delete, lock, change category, status or permissions, export or link them.
fa-pencil::Edit opens the edit page. The view page shows Goals, Conclusion and Notes as three tiles under the title.
fa-ellipsis-vertical::Duplicate, Lock and Timestamp are buttons; the three dots hold changelog, Transfer ownership, Archive and Delete.
imageAlt: The Experiments page: search box, filters, layout buttons and the list of experiments with their category, status and tags
purpose: Keep every experiment in one searchable place, from the first idea to the finished record.
uses: Start a new experiment from a similar one with Duplicate.
Filter by status and owner to see what is still running.
news: Experiments can be organised in folders, linked to orders and resources, and read in a table of contents.
shot: The Experiments list with the search bar, a few experiments ticked, and the bulk-action bar open

title: Resources
summary: Where your team keeps records that are not experiments, such as meetings or equipment, and how to find and use them.
details: fa-cubes-stacked::Open Resources from the top bar or the dashboard. Create opens the same window as for experiments.
fa-magnifying-glass::Search with the same filters and sorting as experiments; the list has the same layout buttons.
fa-square-check::Tick several to archive, delete, lock, change category or status, export or link them.
fa-pencil::Edit has the same text, toolbar and sections as an experiment. Duplicate copies a resource.
fa-calendar-plus::Book item opens the scheduler, only when an admin has switched Bookable resources on (Admin panel, Team, Features).
fa-link::Link resources from an experiment’s Links section so anyone can follow the trail.
imageAlt: The Resources page: search box, filters and the list of resources with their category
purpose: Keep the shared records of the lab in one place that anyone can search and link to.
uses: One resource per group meeting, linked from the experiments that came out of it.
Book an instrument.
news: Resources can be organised in folders, linked to experiments and orders, and found from the left sidebar.
shot: The Resources list with a few resources, and one open with its toolbar

title: Layouts of the lists
summary: See experiments and resources as cards, compact rows, rows with preview, a board by status or a table.
details: fa-table-cells-large::The buttons above the list switch Cards, Compact rows, Rows with preview, Board by status and Tabular.
fa-list::Compact rows is one line per entry, grouped by month. Rows with preview shows the entry you pick beside the list; move with the arrow keys.
fa-table-columns::Board by status has a column for each status. Tabular is a table you can sort.
fa-thumbtack::Pinned entries come first in their own Pinned group in every layout.
fa-floppy-disk::The layout is saved with your account, for experiments and resources separately.
imageAlt: The row of layout buttons above the experiments list, next to the sort buttons, with the list below
purpose: Choose the view that suits the job: a quick scan, a preview while you read, or a board to follow progress.
uses: Compact rows to scan a long list.
Board by status to see what is running and what is done.
news: New: five layouts for the lists, saved per user.

title: Dashboard
summary: The first page: four tiles, your experiments and resources, announcements and Create buttons.
details: fa-gauge::The tiles show experiments and resources changed this week and your open steps and tasks. A tile opens what it counts.
fa-tags::The category and status chips show how many entries each has. Press one to list them; empty ones are dimmed.
fa-plus::Each card has a Create button. For Announcements it is for admins and opens the Announcements tab of the Admin panel.
fa-magnifying-glass::The search box on a card searches experiments or resources.
imageAlt: The dashboard with four tiles of your own activity, then cards for experiments, resources and announcements
purpose: Start the day with what changed and what is waiting for you.
uses: Press Open steps to see what you still have to do.
Press a status chip to list those entries.
news: New: tiles, counts on the chips and one Create button on every card.

title: Create an experiment or resource
summary: One Create window everywhere: type, title, folder and an optional template.
details: fa-plus::Press Create on the dashboard or a list, use the plus in the top bar, or New experiment or New resource in Ctrl+K.
fa-folder::Folder: Unfiled is first. My folders, Bookmarked and All folders narrow the list; New folder makes one on the spot.
fa-clock-rotate-left::It starts on the folder you have open, or the one you used last. Starting from a template, your folder choice wins.
fa-pencil::The new entry opens in edit mode.
imageAlt: The Create dialog with the Experiment, Resource and template tabs, the title field and the Folder chooser
purpose: Start new work in the right place from the first moment.
uses: Open a project folder and press Create: the folder is chosen.
Press Ctrl+K and type New experiment.
news: New: a Folder choice in the Create window on every page.

title: Print a label
summary: Print labels for tubes and boxes on the lab’s label printer, one per row of a pasted table if you like.
details: fa-print::Open the plus in the top bar and choose Print a label. Pick a format, type up to eight lines and press Print.
fa-brackets-curly::Write a name in curly brackets, for example {sample}, where a value changes: it becomes a box you fill in.
fa-bold::Format each line: size, bold, italic, left, centre or right. The preview shows dashed lines for the margins.
fa-table::To print many labels, paste cells from a spreadsheet and click the columns you want. Each row is one label.
fa-gear::Admins set the printer address, port, resolution and formats in Admin panel, Labels. Without a printer address nothing prints.
imageAlt: The Print a label window: format, text size, copies, preview with margins, text lines and a box for pasted table cells
purpose: Label samples without a separate label program.
uses: Print a row of tube labels from a table.
Ask an admin to add a format for a new label size.
news: New: Print a label in the plus menu, and the Labels tab for admins.

title: Google Calendar and Tasks
summary: Send your tasks to a Google calendar, show Google calendars beside your projects and keep your choices everywhere.
details: fa-gear::Calendar settings (the gear in the To-do panel): working hours, weekend days, Google settings, web calendars and a private link.
fa-link::In the Calendars menu of the calendar page, link a project to a Google calendar. Its tasks go there; a calendar chosen for one task wins.
fa-eye::The Calendars menu also chooses which projects and Google calendars are shown.
fa-floppy-disk::Your view, hidden projects and Google choices are saved with your account. The Google sign-in stays in the browser.
fa-list-check::Google Tasks sync is optional and off; an admin must set GOOGLE_SYNC_CSP=true and restart. Tested only with a stand-in for Google.
imageAlt: The Calendar settings window opened from the gear in the To-do panel, with working hours, the Google section with Connect Google, calendars from a web address and the private link
purpose: See your lab tasks next to the rest of your day.
uses: Link a project to its own Google calendar.
Hide a project’s tasks from the calendar page.
news: New: link a project to a Google calendar, choose the calendar of each task, and keep the choices per user.

title: Print and PDF
summary: Print or export an entry, or only the sections you pick, with spreadsheets drawn like the grid on screen.
purpose: Hand over a clean copy of an experiment, or just the part someone needs.
uses: Tick the Results in Contents and press PDF.
When a table is wider than the page, pick Fit to page width, Landscape or Actual size in the question that appears.
details: fa-print::Contents panel header: Print and PDF take the whole entry, or only the sections ticked in Select mode.
fa-file-pdf::The Export menu has the same PDF window (Export as PDF). In the editor, File > Print everything or Print main text.
fa-table::You choose how wide tables print: fit, landscape or split. Remember my choice skips the question; Change wide table setting brings it back.
Sheets print like the live grid: grid lines, labels, fills and bold. Empty trailing rows, columns and hidden ones are left out.
Ctrl+P cannot ask: it uses your remembered choice or fit. Firefox fits wide tables to portrait; the PDF file has landscape pages.
news: New: Print and PDF ask how to print wide tables.
imageAlt: The Contents panel in Select mode with two sections ticked; Print and PDF sit in its header

title: Pins
summary: Pin an entry to keep it at the top of your lists, in its own Pinned group.
purpose: Keep the few entries you use every day within reach.
uses: Pin the protocol you open every morning.
Pin a running experiment.
details: fa-thumbtack::Press the pin on an entry, in a list or on its page. A pinned pin is amber and tilted; the same button unpins.
Pinned entries come first, in a Pinned group, in every list layout and on the first page whatever the sorting.
In rows, the pin of an unpinned entry shows when you point at the row.
On Orders, Pinned for all (shared with the team) and Reference (only you) work like pins. Board cards have Pin to top in their ⋮ menu.
news: New: the Pinned group and a clearer pin.
imageAlt: The first experiment of the list with its pin icon filled in; pinned entries stay at the top of the list

title: Team settings for admins
summary: The admin Team tab shows settings as boxed cards, with a search box, usage tiles and switches for optional features.
purpose: Find and change your team’s settings quickly.
uses: Type “order” in Find a setting.
Switch on Bookable resources for the instruments.
details: fa-user-gear::Open Admin panel > Team. The usage tiles at the top count experiments, resources and users; Generate report exports them.
fa-magnifying-glass::Find a setting: type a word and only the matching settings stay visible. No setting matches says nothing was found.
Settings sit in boxed cards (Experiments, Resources, Orders ...), each with a switch and a short help text.
Features: Tools menu switches (Compounds and Chemical structure editor on; OpenCloning, Inventory off) and Bookable resources (off).
Orders: automatic status steps (Ordered to Collected on a matched shop sheet is on by default) and auto-archive rules.
news: New: boxed cards, a Find a setting box and a Features section.
imageAlt: The Admin panel Team tab with the Configure your team settings and their on/off switches

title: The What’s new popup
summary: A small window after login lists the features you have not seen yet.
purpose: Hear about new features once, without hunting for them.
uses: Press “and N more” to open the full What’s new page.
Switch it off if you do not want it.
details: fa-star::Once after you sign in, only when there is something new since you last saw it, the most important first.
Got it, the X, Esc or a click outside all count as seen, in every browser.
fa-link::“and N more” opens the What’s new page; the small i buttons in the app open the same cards one at a time.
fa-toggle-off::“Don’t show these popups” turns it off. Settings > Appearance > What’s new has the switch to turn it back on.
news: New: the popup itself.
imageAlt: Settings, Appearance tab: the switch “Show a popup with the new features after login” that turns the popup on or off

title: Deadline reminders
summary: A small clock chip, top right, counts the tasks due soon and folds away by itself.
purpose: Be reminded of deadlines without a banner covering the page.
uses: Click the chip to see what is due.
Dismiss all once you have read them.
details: fa-clock::The chip with a number sits at the top right, under the top bar. It moves aside if something is in the way.
Click it to open the list; a step links to its experiment. It folds by itself after a few seconds, or at once with Esc or Collapse.
Dismiss all clears the list. The chip stays as you left it for the rest of the session.
Set a reminder on a task or step with its deadline: at the deadline or 15 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day or 1 week before.
news: New: a small chip instead of a banner.
imageAlt: The small round reminder chip at the top right of the page with the number of deadlines coming up, and the list it opens
